proof_attempt_summary: The run derived modular same-data observable-envelope coverage, a primitive unequal-history dependent-panel transfer with a residual Bartlett-HAC construction, and a generic strict fitted-weight gain on compact full-interior classes. It also proved that fixed-horizon realized-prediction noise makes the relative separate-versus-pooled gain vanish, while constructive future padding was delivered only for a known-parameter Gaussian-VAR benchmark. The package remained incremental because it did not establish an unknown-parameter realized-prediction procedure or execute the serial-dependence/scpi comparison needed to demonstrate practical field-level impact.
tldr: Observable product envelopes give honest simultaneous inference for the fitted-weight component under named coupling, covariance, simulation, and localization events. A primitive fixed-design geometrically beta-mixing panel class supplies explicit conditional coupling and residual-HAC budgets, with coupling order \((\log n_\star)n_\star^{-1/24}\). Finite curvature fallback keeps computation honest on every draw; finite-cap certificates succeed on compact full-interior classes under the stated simulation-growth regime. There, separate regions have a strictly shorter root-\(n_\star\) fitted-weight half-width than identically corrected pooled regions. For realized fixed-horizon prediction, exact Gaussian future noise forces order-one padding, so the relative width gain vanishes. A known-parameter Gaussian-VAR benchmark supplies explicit simultaneous future padding; general realized prediction still needs a separately verified future event.
gap: The verified primary-source anchor, CFPT arXiv:2210.05026v5 (February 1, 2025), Supplement S.2.3, pp. 4–6, equations (S.2.1)–(S.2.2), defines the separate block restrictions, proves their algebraic implication of the pooled restriction, and reports possible shortening, but says the main argument does not justify the product simulation and leaves strong approximation for future work. A renewed public-source search through September 22, 2026 located the Review of Economics and Statistics main article, the same arXiv supplement, scpi documentation/JSS materials, and later staggered-SC papers, but no theorem validating this same separate-product calibration. The primitive fitted-residual unequal-history covariance transfer and the realized-prediction usefulness boundary also remain unproved.
fill: Prove deterministic localization and fixed-oracle quantile domination for arbitrary laws on named events; derive marginal conditional coupling and covariance events from a fixed-design, geometrically mixing primitive panel using the exact residual Bartlett estimator; certify computation; prove corrected pooled containment and strict separated-interior root-n gain; and establish by exact Gaussian inversion the order-one future-padding lower bound for fixed-horizon realized prediction.
